liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Passenger** (3 reviews): Second-set opening jam runs without Jerry; he joins about halfway through Passenger and plays fiercely; Jerry played fiercely on entering because his guitar had troubled him all night; once fixed, he made up for lost time [19][21][28]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Brent is hard to hear in Playin' after he switches to electric piano; The spacey jam in Playin' is called killer [29][30]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Opens the show with a really hot version [27]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Very sweet version; a listener shouts encouragement to Jerry about his singing [27]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 other source): Uploader calls this a noteworthy version [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-05.naks.mason.129756.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 189 min [1]
- **gd81-03-05.wise.lutch.3920.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 169 min; rated 3.86/5 by 22 [4]. Said about its sound: Wise audience tape is crowded with noise and sounds like a cell phone to this reviewer; Disputes the cell-phone complaint; Playin', Althea, To Lay Me Down, Scarlet and the jam sound pretty good, though not the best; Attendee says Jerry's guitar tone was great all evening [23][24][28]
- **gd1981-03-05.174921.Bernstein.MasterCassettes.t-flac2496**: source not stated; 23 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [8]
- **gd1981-03-05.nak700.taylor-radnor.gross.gems.83494.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [9]. Said about its sound: Nak 700 Taylor-Radnor copy is cleaner than the Wise tape, with lower levels, less distortion and less crowd noise [29]
- **gd1981-03-05.169227.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 193 min [10]
- **gd81-03-05.set2-sbd.fink.14024.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 96 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [15]. Said about its sound: Set 2 soundboard is decent but not great; audience version may sound better to those who like audience tapes [22]

## Around the show

- The Stanley Theater is tiny; the loge hangs nearly over the soundboard pit [19]
- Reviewer watched Jerry's guitar problems unfold from the orchestra pit [21]
- Small theater with a Steal Your Face banner and slogan displayed outside [24]
- Taper appears to have been centered, possibly in the front row of the balcony [8]
- Reviewer says the Jim Wise audience version is far better than the set 2 soundboard, which sounds poor [20]
- Much tighter than the sloppy Uptown Theater shows a week earlier, with good vocals and inspired ensemble playing [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-05.naks.mason.129756.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes, with Nakamichi microphones; Transferred on Mason's restored Nak550 [1]
- **gd81-03-05.wise.lutch.3920.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421>D5 set up loge center [4]. Also: Analog source came from Bill Pafford, a friend who attended with taper Jim Wise, who recorded this run [19]
- **gd1981-03-05.174921.Bernstein.MasterCassettes.t-flac2496**: taped by Master Cassettes Recorded by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer & Mastering by Ray Ackerman Edited w/ add'l Mastering by Joe Noel September 23, 2025; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > ?? Deck > Master Cassettes [8]. Also: Source is Bob Wagner's master audience cassettes, Nakamichi 700 mics into a Sony TC-D5M on Maxell XLII-S90 tape [8]
- **gd1981-03-05.nak700.taylor-radnor.gross.gems.83494.flac16**: taped by Mason Taylor and Mark Radnor; transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: NAK 700 (shotgun capsules) > Nak 550 Cassette Recorder > Maxell Metal > HHB Porta-a-DAT [9]. Also: Soundboard and Jim Wise audience tapes patched small gaps in Minglewood, a drums tape flip and an Around and Around glitch [9]
- **gd1981-03-05.169227.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S90) [10]
- **gd81-03-05.set2-sbd.fink.14024.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [15]

Taper appears to have been centered, possibly in the front row of the balcony
Soundboard and Jim Wise audience tapes patched small gaps in Minglewood, a drums tape flip and an Around and Around glitch
Uploader calls this a noteworthy version
Bob Wagner's master cassettes transferred by Charlie Miller; a Jim Vita Nakamichi 500 source patches 22 seconds of Drums
